name: Sacheerome Ltd
tagline: Rs ~1,140-1,190 Cr NSE-SME B2B fragrance & flavour house on a 'brief-to-formulation' model -- ROCE ~36-39% (35.7% FY26), debt-free, revenue growth accelerating (Rs 64 Cr FY22 -> Rs 152 Cr FY26, FY26 +41% YoY), OPM 13% -> 26%, Mukul Agarwal AIF holder (though FII+DII holding has nearly halved since listing) -- genuine, execution-proven quality, but a small F&F TAM, a ~3.6x capacity build, and a stock now ~5x issue price / ~41x earnings after a second big re-rating leg since first review
business_overview: Sacheerome (NSE SME, listed Jun-2025) is a specialised B2B fragrance & flavour (F&F) formulator founded 1992 by Mr. Manoj Arora. It works on a 'brief-to-formulation' model -- corporate FMCG and D2C brands hand over a brief, Sacheerome's R&D (~2.3% of sales) develops the fragrance / flavour, and once approved the formulation is locked into the client's product line, creating annuity-like recurring revenue. It is expanding capacity ~3.6x (7.6 -> 27.6 lakh kg) with ~Rs 184 Cr capex.

fundamentals_narrative: This remains a genuinely high-quality small-cap, and pass-1 confirms execution has been excellent since first flagged: FY26 revenue grew 41% YoY to Rs 152 Cr (four straight years of accelerating growth), EBITDA margin hit 26.02% (beating the ~24% working estimate at first review), PAT jumped 78% to Rs 28.44 Cr, and ROCE held mid-30s% -- all funded almost debt-free. The Reg 31(4) promoter disclosure confirms zero pledge, and promoter holding has been rock-stable at 71.54% since listing, addressing the main governance open question from the first pass. The 'brief-to-formulation' lock-in remains a genuine switching-cost mechanic. What has changed materially is the price: the stock has re-rated a second leg since first review -- P/E ~26x -> ~41x, market cap ~Rs 700-785 Cr -> ~Rs 1,140-1,190 Cr, now ~5x the Rs 102 issue price -- while FII+DII combined holding nearly halved (from ~14.3% just after listing to ~6.5% by Mar-2026) even as public/retail holding rose from ~14% to 22%. That is a soft institutional-selling signal (reason unconfirmed -- could be simple IPO-anchor lock-in expiry rather than a fundamentals call) worth tracking. The original open questions largely resolve in the company's favour: the FY27/28/29 guidance ladder (Rs 200/250/300 Cr) has stayed consistent rather than being walked back, and FY26's delivery came in ahead of the prior conservative-guidance framing. The unresolved ones are: (1) how much of the FY22->FY26 margin gain is durable given part of it traced to an employee-cost cut of unconfirmed sustainability; (2) whether the new 27.6 lakh kg capacity actually gets commissioned and ramped on the guided timeline -- no independent commissioning-status confirmation found this pass; (3) at ~41x trailing, the multiple now already prices in essentially the entire guided growth ladder, leaving little margin of safety versus the first review's ~26x entry.

verdict_headline: A genuinely high-quality, execution-proven B2B fragrance formulator with a sticky model -- but a second re-rating leg (P/E ~26x -> ~41x) into a small TAM and an unconfirmed-status 3.6x capacity build keeps this 'neither' / conviction Medium, with materially less margin of safety than at first review
verdict_reasoning: Aligns with the priority-1 'CDMO / specialty & aroma chemicals' theme (keywords include fragrance, aroma chemical, specialty chemical) -- but it was processed as a tier-4.5 external lead, not a Step-1 discovery theme hit, so theme-ranking is informational here.

four_box score unchanged at 2.5 -> 'neither'. tailwind yes (F&F premiumisation, D2C brand proliferation, import substitution from global majors -- a real multi-year pull, reinforced this pass by >100% guided current-facility utilisation). tam weak (Indian F&F market is a few thousand crore; management's own FY29 guide of ~Rs 300 Cr revenue is far short of what a 10x-in-2-3-yr case needs). moat weak (formulation lock-in and sustained high ROCE are convincing and now execution-proven, but it remains a small player with modest R&D intensity and unproven durability at 3.6x scale). valuation weak-to-worse (~41x FY26 earnings after a SECOND re-rating leg since first review, up from ~26x -- priced as a quality compounder with little room for surprise). No written exception taken.

Deep-dive pass 1 (2026-09-22): business quality is no longer in question -- FY26 delivered +41% revenue, +78% PAT, 26% margin, sustained mid-30s ROCE, no pledge, stable promoter holding. But the stock re-rated in lockstep (and then some): market cap ~Rs 700-785 Cr -> ~Rs 1,140-1,190 Cr, price ~5x issue. FII+DII holding nearly halved since listing while retail piled in -- a soft caution flag, not conclusive. Conviction held at Medium: the improved execution and the richer valuation roughly offset each other. Re-check after FY27 results confirm whether the new capacity is commissioning on schedule and whether the ~41x multiple is being justified by delivery against the Rs 200 Cr FY27 guide.
